pull_request.body:
<!-- uv-active-slice: actions-hardening -->
<!-- uv-next-slice: project-identity-v2-compat-reader -->

## Goal

Harden maintained GitHub Actions supply-chain and credential boundaries without changing UV Studio runtime or product behavior.

## Changes

- pin every maintained remote Action/reusable-workflow ref to a full 40-character commit SHA; current first-party pins retain human-readable `# v4` / `# v5` comments and use the same revisions previously resolved by the major tags;
- keep every workflow top-level at `permissions: contents: read`;
- keep read-only checkout credentials disabled with explicit `persist-credentials: false`;
- narrow the only approved write authority to the single `vendor` job in `vendor-videoclaw.yml`, where authenticated checkout is required for the real branch push;
- freeze the complete parsed semantic YAML structure of the sole write-authorized workflow against a reviewed canonical contract instead of interpreting shell text;
- enforce a reviewed execution allowlist: only the four current exact pinned Node Actions (`checkout`, `setup-python`, `setup-node`, `upload-artifact`) may be invoked;
- reject repository-local `uses: ./...`, all job-level reusable workflows, Docker actions without an immutable policy, and any new/unreviewed remote Action until a separate transitive security review extends the policy;
- add permanent PyYAML-structural guards for unexpected write authority, duplicate YAML keys, checkout credential-policy drift and case-colliding checkout input keys;
- keep pinned `PyYAML==6.0.2` in the development/test layer only; bootstrap proves the core import/compile contract before installing it for the unit/security suite.

## Verification

Six fresh ordinary-ChatGPT semantic reviews found successive concrete P2 fail-open cases in earlier guard implementations. All six were classified CONFIRMED and materially fixed:

1. text/regex matching could miss valid flow-style job permissions and accept a credential decoy outside checkout `with`;
2. the remaining handwritten parser could miss an entire job represented as a YAML flow mapping;
3. case-sensitive Action/checkout recognition could be bypassed through mixed-case GitHub repository identity;
4. checkout `with:` keys were treated case-sensitively even though GitHub Runner binds action inputs case-insensitively;
5. the writer-liveness helper inferred shell execution from text, so `git push -n` and non-executed heredoc content could satisfy the supposed real-push predicate;
6. repository-local `uses: ./...` could hide floating transitive remote Actions inside a composite Action or local reusable workflow.

The fifth fix removes shell interpretation entirely by freezing the parsed semantic structure of the sole writer workflow. The sixth fix fails closed on local delegation; a bounded follow-up self-audit applies the same transitive principle to remote execution by allowlisting only the four exact current Action SHAs. Their pinned `action.yml` metadata was re-read and all four use `runs.using: node20`, not composite nested `uses`.

All prior review results are stale because material fixes followed them. The final exact BASE/HEAD requires one fresh ordinary-ChatGPT semantic review plus all five permanent exact-head CI checks before merge.

## Architecture impact

No product/runtime/frontend/canonical application authority changes. `requirements-uv.txt` remains unchanged; PyYAML is test/development tooling only.

## Known limitations

The official connector exposes `mark_pull_request_ready_for_review`, but repeated live invocation on predecessor draft PR #85 failed because the connector GraphQL response selection queries nonexistent `Repository.fullDatabaseId`. PR #85 was closed unmerged and the same branch was reopened directly non-draft as PR #86; no privileged repository fallback is introduced.

New/local/reusable Actions are intentionally denied by the current guard. Supporting one later requires an explicit reviewed extension of the transitive execution allowlist.

The existing timing-sensitive `ProductionWorkspacePanel` remount race remains separate and unchanged.

## Next task

After this slice merges and lifecycle-closes, enable the repository-level full-SHA Actions policy when available, then resume `project-identity-v2-compat-reader` from the accepted D-070 migration inventory.

A material fix is required, so this review becomes stale for any later head.

REVIEW_RESULT_V1 received for exact `66410db447c896fb898636634258402fae1edbff..2618046496c8a44aa018d745ccdcfacf3af3f28e`: status=FINDINGS, review_validity=CURRENT, reported_findings=1, rejected_candidates=4, review_context=ordinary_chat_fresh. The reported P2 (checkout `with:` input keys are case-insensitive in GitHub Runner but were validated case-sensitively by the permanent guard) is classified CONFIRMED. The fix normalizes checkout input keys with `casefold()` before credential validation and rejects case-colliding logical duplicates such as `persist-credentials` plus `PERSIST-CREDENTIALS`; a regression test covers the reported bypass. This material fix invalidates the reviewed head, so a fresh exact-head ordinary-ChatGPT review is required before merge.

Semantic review finding on reviewed head `750829da9cdc4039a3761a979313743baeb23535`: **CONFIRMED (P2)**. `_run_contains_real_git_push` treated shell text as execution evidence and accepted `git push -n` (Git short form of `--dry-run`), with the same class of false positive possible for non-executed heredoc content. Material fix follows this reviewed head, so this review is now **STALE_MATERIAL_CHANGE**. Resolution: remove the shell heuristic entirely and freeze the complete parsed semantic structure of the sole write-authorized `vendor-videoclaw.yml` against a reviewed canonical writer-workflow contract. Regression coverage explicitly rejects long/short dry-run push, heredoc push text, and a disabled push step.

Independent semantic review for exact 66410db447c896fb898636634258402fae1edbff..b709de941f7444c6cf71296d54eef0d6bd9f4261 reported one P2: repository-local `uses: ./...` could bypass the permanent remote-ref guard through a composite Action or local reusable workflow with transitive floating remote `uses`. Development classification: CONFIRMED. Current maintained workflows do not use local `uses`. The material fix fails closed on all step-level and job-level repository-local `uses` until a separate reviewed transitive immutable-reference policy exists, with dedicated regression coverage. This review is stale for the new head.
